title: Wrangler config binds the required D1, KV, and R2 resources

claim.statement: The Worker's wrangler configuration binds a D1 database as DB, a KV namespace as CACHE, and an R2 bucket as ASSETS, each with a non-empty resource identifier, as the design's resource table requires.

question.instructions: The state is the bindings section of a Cloudflare wrangler configuration as JSON. Binding names are case-sensitive and must match exactly. Check every condition: (1) the d1_databases array contains an entry whose binding is exactly "DB" with a non-empty database_id; (2) the kv_namespaces array contains an entry whose binding is exactly "CACHE" with a non-empty id; (3) the r2_buckets array contains an entry whose binding is exactly "ASSETS" with a non-empty bucket_name. Do all three conditions hold?

notes: SUPERSEDED (kept for the record, not assurance-eligible): Laya scored this three-binding rule near chance. The check is now owned by the validator rubric RUB-S1-VAL-WRANGLER-REQUIRED-BINDINGS (validator-wrangler-required-bindings.rubric.json), which reads JSONC or TOML and decides it exactly. Do not bind new claims to this rubric.

Measured on the pinned checkpoint, CPU fp32, eval mode, one state per forward pass: formulation `noul_tight`, held-out accuracy 0.606 (n=180); ECE (15 bins) 0.347 raw logits, 0.232 at the checkpoint's shipped temperature, 0.089 at the fitted temperature 5.342; at verify 0.90 / refute 0.90, coverage 0.017 (VERIFIED 0, REFUTED 3, INCONCLUSIVE 177) with precision 1.000. Calibration split ECE after fitting 0.085 (n=180). Dataset: test/fixtures/system1-calibration/wrangler-bindings/ (report: docs/calibration/system1-calibration-report.md).

Formulations tried (held-out accuracy at fitted T): noul_verbatim 0.517, noul_tight 0.606, noul_neutral_labels 0.511, choice2_neutral 0.506, choice2_tight 0.506, typed_choice2_neutral 0.522. Controls at the fitted T: CTL-WRANGLER-ALL-BOUND VERIFIED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.652); CTL-WRANGLER-NO-R2 REFUTED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.708); CTL-WRANGLER-WRONG-KV-NAME REFUTED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.657). Replay: 9 runs per control (6 in fresh processes), max thresholded-probability delta 0, max logit delta 0; epsilon is 10x the larger of the measured delta and the delta implied by the worst logit wobble seen on any checkpoint (2.99e-4, laya-multilingual under concurrent CPU load), rounded up.

Temperature semantics: `calibration.temperature` replaces the checkpoint's own temperature for this question's (type, option count) bucket, i.e. probabilities are softmax(option logits / T); a runner sets agent.temperature_by_options[temp_bucket] = T and passes no `lang`, so lang_temperatures cannot override it. `measured_ece` is the larger of the calibration-split (in-sample) and held-out test-split ECE at the fitted temperature.

Not assurance-eligible: controls land on the wrong status: CTL-WRANGLER-ALL-BOUND, CTL-WRANGLER-NO-R2, CTL-WRANGLER-WRONG-KV-NAME; held-out precision rests on only 3 gated verdicts (3 correct; Wilson 95% lower bound 0.44). Thresholds were not lowered to compensate; this rubric may back diagnostic runs only until a re-authored version measures inside the bar.

The extractor keeps only the three binding arrays so the state fits the 320-token state budget of the 512-context checkpoint; a config whose bindings exceed it is ERROR `input_over_context_limit`, never truncated.

Honest limit: exact binding names are decidable by a JSON parser, and a parser test is stronger evidence than any model. Use this rubric only where the plan states binding requirements in prose that a fixed parser does not encode; otherwise the Planning Test Engineer should select a test, not a System One backend.
